name: block-inventory trigger queries
description: Should trigger when the user wants a survey of the blocks authors could use: the repo's own blocks plus standard Block Collection blocks, with one-line purposes, typically before content modeling or import. Near misses: looking up one specific block, building a block, content modeling, finding pages, import itself.

queries.query: Before we import the pricing page, list which blocks our repo already has and which standard ones from Adobe's Block Collection we could add, with a one-line description of each.
What blocks can authors use on this site? Give me a list with what each one is for in plain author language, including standard ones we don't have yet.
I'm about to decide how to structure a landing page. Give me the block palette first: what we have locally and what the Block Collection offers.
Make an inventory of our block library for the content team's onboarding doc: each block, what it does, and a live example link where there is one.
List every block in this repository with a one-line purpose each, so the content team knows what exists.
Does Adobe have a reference `modal` block we can copy into the repo? Find it and tell me where it lives.
Authors will write a new `stats` block as a table: a number column and a label column, one row per stat. Write the decorate function and CSS for that block so it works with exactly that markup.
We need a testimonials block. Propose the content model: what an author types into the table, which cells are optional, and how it behaves with one or five quotes.
Which existing pages on our site already use the `cards` block, and with which variants? I want to test a change against them.
Import https://www.example.com/pricing into our EDS site as a new page.
`aem up` dies immediately with EADDRINUSE and I have no idea what is on the port. How do I get the dev server running?
Please review PR #214 on our EDS repo. Someone added a tabs block and I want to make sure it follows our conventions. Just leave comments, don't push changes.
